original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Exact paid-factor minimum for general (non-diagonal) targets in the right-vector alphabet I + u y^T (u in R^n, y in K^n) with free GL_n(K) maps: tests the formula min_T dim_K (M T - I) K^n proposed in open question 1 of #4243 on every target over eleven small (algebra, n) domains.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a larger or nonabelian register model escapes the scoped three-register obstruction. This package answers a narrower open question left by #4243: whether its diagonal count extends to all targets. The answer is no for the noncommutative algebra M2(F2), and the trailing free map is necessary even over commutative non-local algebras.
bottleneck_link: A legal target cheaper than its column bound would be a new bit primitive; this package shows the column bound is attained on ten commutative domains and is not attained in general. Kappa is unchanged.
stop_rule: Exhaust every target on small algebras, record each place the formula or its no-free-map form fails, independently confirm one failure, then stop.
evidence: verify.py --stage main and --stage large compute exact minima by breadth-first search over all words and the formula by enumerating every T in GL_n(K), on 343,810 targets in total. Formula failures: 72, all over M2(F2) at n=2 (cost 3, formula 2). No-free-map gaps: 2 over F2xF2, 6 over F2[C3], 684 over M2(F2). The transposition witness is rechecked in M_4(F_2) by a separate enumeration of all two- and three-factor products.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does the formula hold for every commutative K-algebra, or every local algebra with residue field K?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It holds on all ten commutative domains checked here, which include the group algebras F2[C2], F2[C3] and F3[C2]-type products.
open_questions.first_step: Prove the one-step peeling condition A x1 in A(H R) + x1 R for a minimizing T, starting with local R.
open_questions.blocked_by: No general factorization argument is proved here.

open_questions.question: Does the M2(F2) failure lift to a nonabelian group algebra such as F2[S3]?
open_questions.why_it_matters: #4243 covers diagonals in every F2[G]; a failure inside F2[S3] would bound how far its count extends for nonabelian registers.
open_questions.first_step: Fix an explicit K-algebra isomorphism F2[S3] = F2[C2] x M2(F2) and project words onto the matrix block.
open_questions.blocked_by: The isomorphism and projection argument are not checked here.

open_questions.question: What is the exact cost for noncommutative algebras?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The formula undercounts M2(F2) targets by one at n=2.
open_questions.first_step: Compare cost with the K^2n rank of M - I in the Morita picture M_n(M_2(K)) = M_2n(K).
open_questions.blocked_by: Only n=2 over M2(F2) is enumerated.
